transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-09-03
Start Time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Samir Das (Tailwind CTO); Nora Li (Tailwind ML Eng); Ben Winters (Tailwind SRE)

Auto Summary:
Week 4 POC: tuned kernel selection (hybrid path), reduced median TTFT from ~120ms to ~85ms on test cluster; streaming latency improved for steady-state but spikes remain during multi-request microbursts. Action: run bounded-seqlen microburst tests, share traces, and provide Dedicated pricing for burst capacity.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick agenda — results, triage, experiments and next steps. is the time still good for you all?
00:06 Samir Das: yeah good for me, nods, we have a hard cutover window next tuesday so want to understand risk
00:12 Nora Li: also want to make sure we report good numbers to infra, last week's TTFT table had some outliers
00:18 Ravi Patel: great — i'll walk through the kernel swap numbers first. quick note, transcript is fuzzy in places
00:26 Ravi Patel: ok so baseline on host path (open-model v2, fp16) median first token 118 to 125 ms depending on seqlen mix, p95 around 260ms. after hybrid kernel switch (stream-first + slab fallback) median dropped to 84 ms, p95 to ~190ms in the test bench
00:45 Ben Winters: those look promising, what's the test config? batch size and kv state?
00:50 Ravi Patel: synthetic steady-state with warm KV cache, per-request batch 1, continuous batching enabled but limited to 40ms queue window. seq len distro: 60% <=128, 30% 129-512, 10% >512. microburst sim used burst of 200 concurrent short requests.
01:12 Samir Das: our production trace has more 3-5 token completions that are latency sensitive, so first-byte is everything, can we replicate that
01:20 Nora Li: we dropped a trace sample in the drive, i will upload 10k traces — some are skewed toward 10-20 token replies
01:28 Maya Chen: perfect, please send the trace. ravi — did you try the bounded sequence cap approach we discussed?
01:34 Ravi Patel: yes, quick check: capping at 256 dropped p95 in microbursts by ~25% but the median bumped slightly because longer replies get truncated and we had to stitch in a follow-up. noisy tradeoff
01:48 Samir Das: stitching is okay if it's seamless to client, but latency for the user matters — we prefer fewer round trips
01:55 Ben Winters: question re: dedicated tier — if we move to Dedicated can we get lower variance or just more throughput?
02:01 Maya Chen: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and you can reserve burst pools; you'll also control kernel pinning and can lock quantized variants. pricing differs for sustained vs burst capacity.
02:12 Samir Das: can you send that in writing (pricing + SLA for burst)?
02:15 Maya Chen: yes i'll include two pricing scenarios — reserved baseline and baseline + burst buffer with pre-warm guarantee
02:21 Ravi Patel: back to tuning — kernel selection changed the steady path to more vectorized attention kernels which helped single-token latency, but we saw regression on throughput for long sequences in one kernel variant. we added a fallback that routes >512 tokens to the slab kernel
02:40 Nora Li: that fallback sounds good. are there telemetry gaps we need to close to make routing safe?
02:46 Ravi Patel: good point — we need per-request seqlen tag in the trace and better token-level timing. current trace shows request start/end but not per-token timings; we can add a lightweight timing hook in the SDK
03:01 Ben Winters: any security blockers for adding that hook? our compliance team will ask about PII in traces
03:07 Maya Chen: we recommend hashing and redacting content in traces; Redwood supports KMS encryption for logs and you can route traces to your storage
03:15 Samir Das: ok we'll follow that pattern
03:18 Maya Chen: on microburst hedging, we discussed hedging to a lower-capacity, lower-cost model vs hedging to a faster variant. any preference?
03:25 Nora Li: prefer hedging to a fast path when latencies are user facing, but hedging to a cheaper path for non-critical batched jobs
03:32 Ravi Patel: note that hedging increases tokens generated and potentially costs, so we need to estimate unit economics. also warm vs cold KV matters — hedged requests may miss cache
03:45 Samir Das: can we quantify cost delta for hedging strategy A (fast model) vs B (cheaper model)?
03:51 Maya Chen: yes i'll include a small calc in the follow-up: expected extra tokens and cost per 1k requests, plus expected latency gains
03:58 Ben Winters: during last test we saw microburst p99 up to 1.2s — is that still the case after the kernel swap
04:04 Ravi Patel: p99 improved to ~760ms in our bench but with cold KV or simultaneous bursts it can spike above 1s
04:12 Nora Li: we suspect our production mix has more short requests which makes KV warm more often — that might help
04:18 Maya Chen: two experiments agreed: A) bounded seqlen microburst at 128/256/512 to map p metrics; B) toggle continuous batching windows (20ms/40ms/80ms) to see tradeoffs. Ravi will run A on the test cluster, Nora will provide the trace and Ben will run an infra smoke test on staging
04:36 Ravi Patel: i'll also run a quick quantization profile (int8 dynamic) on the dedicated replicate and compare TTFT; note quant helps throughput but sometimes regresses first-token due to dequant op cost
04:50 Samir Das: interesting — so quant may save us cost on sustained loads but could hurt UI latency
04:55 Maya Chen: correct, that's why we include per-route controls to use quant for background jobs only
05:02 Nora Li: about the SDK timing hook — does Redwood's console ingest support per-token timing or just aggregated? the console currently shows per-request and per-token cost but not timing every token
05:12 Ravi Patel: console can accept per-token timing but we need to enable it in the pipeline; there's a small perf overhead though
05:20 Ben Winters: we probably want to enable it for a short window of experiments, not always
05:24 Maya Chen: agreed
05:28 Samir Das: curious — what's the rollback plan again if we pin kernels in Dedicated and see throughput regression?
05:33 Ravi Patel: simple rollback: automated canary for 10% traffic, metric linting on RT/p95/p99, immediate fallback to previous kernel bundle if >10% regression in throughput or >20% increase in p99. we also keep a standby fallback model in hosted path
05:48 Nora Li: ok sounds safe
05:50 Maya Chen: any blockers from compliance for Dedicated or Private options early in the pilot?
05:55 Ben Winters: compliance wants SOC 2 type 2 evidence and audit logs for any managed logs we ship. also they asked about SSO/SAML and RBAC for console access
06:03 Maya Chen: Redwood can provide SOC 2 docs and enterprise SSO; we'll include Security datasheet in the follow-up
06:10 Samir Das: timeline: we need to pick path by next monday (2026-09-07) to align with change window
06:15 Maya Chen: understood — next meeting we'll present bounded microburst results, pricing, and quantization impact. is friday good for a short sync or should we keep to monday?
06:23 Samir Das: friday better for us — gives us time to run internal infra checks
06:28 Maya Chen: ok friday sync tentatively 2026-09-04 15:00 UTC. i'll send calendar invite
06:32 Ben Winters: small note — our infra team prefers not to enable per-token timing in prod, so we'll coordinate
06:36 Nora Li: i'll upload traces right after this
06:39 Maya Chen: cool, thanks. quick recap: Ravi runs bounded seqlen microburst (128/256/512) and quant bench; Nora uploads 10k trace; Maya sends pricing + security docs; Ben runs staging smoke test. follow-ups due early next week
06:55 Samir Das: thanks all
06:58 Maya Chen: thanks everyone, see you friday

End of transcript
